detailed_summary: The paper addresses a conjecture by Tang and Zhang concerning the optimal constant $c_p(m)$ in a norm inequality for sums of complex matrices. Specifically, for $p\geq 1$ and $m\geq 2$, the inequality bounds the $p$-norm of a sum of matrices by a constant times the $p$-norm of the sum of their absolute values. Tang and Zhang conjectured a closed-form expression for $c_p(m)$, derived from a family of common-left equiangular rank-one matrices. The paper rigorously disproves this conjecture for all $m\geq 2$ and all $1<p<2$. The authors provide a counterexample family and demonstrate that the conjectured constant is not valid in this parameter range. The paper is concise (5 pages) and focuses on a specific technical result in matrix analysis and operator theory.

Provides an explicit counterexample family of matrices that violates the conjectured inequality.
Establishes a new lower bound for $c_p(m)$ in the range $1<p<2$, showing the conjectured value is too small.
Clarifies the behavior of the optimal constant in the non-commutative $L_p$ norm inequality, contributing to the theory of matrix norms.
methodology_analysis: The paper employs a constructive counterexample approach. The authors likely construct a specific set of $m$ matrices (possibly rank-one, equiangular) for which the ratio $\|\sum A_k\|_p / \|\sum |A_k|\|_p$ exceeds the conjectured constant. The analysis likely involves explicit computation of the $p$-norms for the constructed matrices, using properties of singular values and the definition of the Schatten $p$-norm. The counterexample is designed to exploit the non-commutativity and the specific structure of the matrices, and the proof likely involves inequalities for $1<p<2$ that differ from the $p\geq 2$ case. The method is direct and rigorous, relying on explicit matrix constructions rather than abstract existence arguments.
